title: Conditional finite-sector mixture Cauchy error bridge
purpose: Give an exact finite-sector bound separating weight drift from component-cylinder drift. The bound is an input contract for a future source-owned full-Q law; it does not define weights, a tail law or a PAH limit.

fixed_scope.carrier_and_path: Use the unchanged PAH-OMC-004 strip and PAH-OMC-010 finite path inherited by PAH-OMC-014. This theorem takes no refinement, cutoff, volume, beta or phase limit.
fixed_scope.finite_index: Use one finite sector index type ι representing a supplied common finite sector block. Growing-Q tails and their mass are not silently identified with this block.
fixed_scope.mixture: M(w,a)=sum_i w_i a_i. For two candidate finite levels, e_w bounds the pointwise weight drift and e_a bounds the pointwise component-cylinder drift.
fixed_scope.source_owner_obligation: A full-Q packet must supply a common index embedding or tail estimate, normalized nonnegative weights with the pointwise bound, component Cauchy errors, and a declared limit in which both e_w and e_a (and any tail term) vanish.

lean.scope: Abstract finite index set and real-valued weights/components; no PAH law or limit instantiated.

assumptions: Every component value at the second level is bounded in absolute value by C.
The first-level weight is pointwise bounded in absolute value by one.
theorem_contract.conclusion: The total finite mixture drift is bounded by card(ι)*(C*e_w+e_a).
not_supplied: No normalized full-Q sector weights or projective kernel.
No common finite index embedding for the growing-Q union or tail-mass estimate.
No PAH-specific e_w/e_a Cauchy rates, topology, boundary estimate or stationarity passage.

non_claims: This theorem does not instantiate mu_(n,R), omega or any sector law.
It does not prove projective consistency, a PAH Cauchy estimate, weak cylinder convergence, positivity/normalization of a global mixture, R-488 nonzero, stationarity, closability or a semigroup.
No physical Pre-A, spacetime, QFT, gravity, Yang--Mills, mass-gap or TOE conclusion follows.
